correctness.rationale: The labeled off-diagonal ordered-pair de Bruijn graph is computed exactly from the Rule 30 local map. Eight recurrent states quotient into four signed vertices with seven complete edges; every closed walk is either a zero self-loop or a concatenation of 11 0^m b blocks. The sum of orientation flips equals the parity of terminal zero bits. Even-parity closed lifts exactly represent distinct indexed predecessor pairs for arbitrary n>=3. A separately implemented brute census checks 131,064 target strings through length 16; finite tests support, but do not replace, the all-length finite graph argument.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General de Bruijn target inversion covers algorithmic computability, but neither provides a shorter intrinsic signed-block description nor asserts the membership equivalence. Homogeneous target counts do not cover heterogeneous target pattern placement.

originality.rationale: The new statement classifies precisely which cyclic output words admit at least two predecessors, using an even-flip signed-block language. Earlier aggregate multiplicity formulas count such outputs but cannot imply their identities; general predecessor algorithms do not contain this explicit intrinsic rule-30 block characterization. The closest full texts were materially inspected. Historical priority remains qualified by unindexed or inaccessible possible equivalents.
residual_risks: Unindexed historical normal-form descriptions may exist, especially within older cellular automata graph terminology.
The 1983 general survey was read as publisher abstract only, not full text; no whole-document noncoverage assertion is made.
A standard general preimage algorithm could indirectly generate the signed-block grammar after specialized minimization, but this specialization was not stated in the inspected literature.

value.rationale: The theorem answers an intrinsic infinite-family inverse ambiguity question at the level of individual cyclic target words, which predecessor-frequency counts do not answer. It exposes the nontrivial orientation-parity obstruction to lifting unordered collision paths and yields a compact regular signed-block description and eight-state O(n) membership algorithm. It does not claim a general inverse-algorithm speed improvement or routine histogram reformulation.
